poll._comment: max_pages 10 covers the whole window the list-tweets endpoint will serve (it ran dry after ~800 posts in the 2026-09-10 backfill), so no gap the endpoint can still answer for is lost when GitHub's cron skips hours — as it did between 07:19 and 09:47 UTC that day. Pages past the boundary are never requested, so an on-cadence poll still costs one partial page.

semantic._comment: Local embedding layer (src/embeddings.js, src/semantic.js; docs/SEMANTIC_MATCHING.md). min_sim: cosine floor for a post to count as near a story; 0.8 was calibrated on the 2026-09-10 probes (nothing Claude judged on-story fell below it) and is a reading floor, not a verdict. candidates: how many nearby stories the classifier is shown per post as similarity hints (it still decides from the text). related_posts: how many unlabeled neighbours the dashboard lists under each emerging card and story row.

stories._comment: Continuous story promotion (src/stories.js --auto-promote / --retire, run nightly after classify). auto_promote: when false, --auto-promote only lists what would be promoted and writes nothing. min_posts, min_members, min_days: a story candidate (placement kind 'story' with a macro) must reach all three — posts, distinct members, distinct days — before it is written to config/taxonomy.yaml as a provisional developing story; taxonomy gaps are never auto-promoted. max_per_night: at most this many promotions per run, most posts first (the rest wait for the next night). retire_after_quiet_days: a provisional story that has been in the taxonomy at least this many days with zero assignments in data/topics over the window is marked retired: true — it leaves the classifier prompt but keeps its key so rollups and history still resolve.

anthropic._comment: Workload identity federation ids for GitHub Actions (public identifiers, not secrets). The rule only accepts OIDC tokens from this repo's main branch. Outside Actions, set CLASSIFIER_ANTHROPIC_API_KEY (or ANTHROPIC_API_KEY) instead.

narrative_lists._comment: Public X Lists the narrative layer may scan (owner: the credential account). role: who is on it; priority 1 = scan first (Democratic side and the press that covers it), 3 = counter-message only. Reads are billed per post returned and go through the daily ledger.
